publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: We find good consistency with the standard spatially-flat 6-parameter ΛCDM cosmology having a power-law spectrum of adiabatic scalar perturbations (denoted “base ΛCDM” in this paper), from polarization, temperature, and lensing, separately and in combination.

span.label: cosmic microwave background anisotropies
span.quote: Since their discovery (Smoot et al. 1992), temperature anisotropies in the cosmic microwave background (CMB) have become one of the most powerful ways of studying cosmology and the physics of the early Universe.

span.label: observational-data-analysis
span.quote: We present cosmological parameter results from the final full-mission Planck measurements of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies, combining information from the temperature and polarization maps and the lensing reconstruction.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE MODEL EVERY NUMBER IN THE PAPER IS QUOTED AGAINST IS INTRODUCED AS A QUOTED LABEL, WITH A PARAMETER COUNT AND A SCOPE: we refer to this model, **WHICH CAN BE SPECIFIED BY SIX PARAMETERS**, as **“BASE” ΛCDM IN THIS PAPER**. The scare quotes and the words `in this paper` are both the collaboration's: the label is declared local to the document, and what it denotes is fixed by a count of parameters rather than by a description
span.quote: We refer to this model, which can be specified by six parameters, as “base” ΛCDM in this paper.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHICH PARAMETERS ARE PRIMITIVE IS STATED AS A CHOICE, NOT AS A FACT ABOUT THE UNIVERSE: the first six parameters are **THE ONES ON WHICH WE IMPOSE FLAT PRIORS AND USE AS SAMPLING PARAMETERS**; the remaining parameters **ARE DERIVED FROM THE FIRST SIX**. The same physics could be parameterised the other way round, and the paper says which way it chose
span.quote: The first six parameters here are the ones on which we impose flat priors and use as sampling parameters; the remaining parameters are derived from the first six.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN ENTIRE CLASS OF PARAMETERS IS NAMED “NUISANCE” IN SCARE QUOTES - AND THE QUOTES COME OFF IN THE NEXT SENTENCE, WHERE THEY ARE SAMPLED ON THE SAME FOOTING AS THE COSMOLOGICAL ONES: a physically motivated parametric model containing **“nuisance” parameters**; **these nuisance parameters ARE SAMPLED, ALONG WITH COSMOLOGICAL PARAMETERS**, during MCMC exploration of the likelihood. The hedge is dropped one sentence after it is made, and the objects it hedged about are treated as first-class
span.quote: a physically motivated parametric model containing “nuisance” parameters. These nuisance parameters are sampled, along with cosmological parameters, during Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) exploration of the likelihood.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A CEILING ON THE PAPER'S OWN INTERPRETATION, STATED BY THE PAPER: a total systematic uncertainty of around half a sigma **MAY BE MORE REALISTIC**, and **VALUES SHOULD NOT BE OVERINTERPRETED BEYOND THIS LEVEL**. Not a limitation of the data but an instruction to the reader about how far the numbers may be read - issued by the people who produced them
span.quote: A total systematic uncertainty of around 0.5σ may be more realistic, and values should not be overinterpreted beyond this level.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: TWO WAYS OF DOING ONE CORRECTION ARE NAMED IN A SINGLE SENTENCE, BY CONTRAST WITH EACH OTHER: adopting the estimates from one spectrum for both (**we call this the “MAP-BASED” APPROACH**); or applying independent estimates from each (**the “SPECTRUM-BASED” APPROACH**). Neither name would mean anything without the other; the pair is defined by the difference between two procedures
span.quote: We have investigated ways of correcting for effective polarization efficiencies: adopting the estimates from EE (which are about a factor of 2 more precise than T E) for both the T E and EE spectra (we call this the “map-based” approach); or applying independent estimates from T E and EE (the “spectrum-based” approach).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE NULL EXPLANATION IS DECLARED THE BASELINE ASSUMPTION, IN THOSE WORDS: alternatively, it could just be a statistical fluctuation, **WHICH IS OUR BASELINE ASSUMPTION**. Which of the competing accounts gets the default is a choice, and it is named as one rather than argued for
span.quote: Alternatively, it could just be a statistical fluctuation, which is our baseline assumption.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: EVIDENCE IS GRANTED AND THE CLAIM IS DECLINED IN THE SAME SENTENCE: although both likelihoods **CLEARLY SHOW A PREFERENCE** for a lensing amplitude above one, **THIS CANNOT BE CLAIMED TO BE A ROBUST DETECTION** at much over two sigma. `Clearly show` and `cannot be claimed` are asserted of the same result, and the line between them is a number
span.quote: Although both likelihoods clearly show a preference for AL > 1, this cannot be claimed to be a robust detection at much over 2σ

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE COLLABORATION CALLS A PERSISTENT ANOMALY IN ITS OWN DATA **A CURIOUS FEATURE**: the preference for a lensing amplitude above one within the model **IS A CURIOUS FEATURE OF THE PLANCK CMB POWER SPECTRUM DATA**, and has already been discussed extensively in three earlier papers, **ALTHOUGH IT IS NOW SLIGHTLY MORE SIGNIFICANT**. A result that has survived three releases, growing, and the standing description of it is an adjective
span.quote: The preference for AL > 1 within the ΛCDM model is a curious feature of the Planck CMB power spectrum data, and has already been discussed extensively in PCP13, PCP15, and Planck Collaboration Int. LI (2017), although it is now slightly more significant.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE AUTHORS CHARACTERISE THEIR OWN REVISION AS **LARGELY COSMETIC**: it is important to emphasize that these changes to the likelihood **ARE LARGELY COSMETIC AND HAVE VERY LITTLE IMPACT ON COSMOLOGICAL PARAMETERS**. The word measures a methodological change by its effect on the outputs rather than by what was changed
span.quote: It is important to emphasize that these changes to the 2018 CamSpec TT likelihood are largely cosmetic and have very little impact on cosmological parameters.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A METHOD CHANGE BETWEEN RELEASES IS STATED AS A DIFFERENCE FROM THE PREVIOUS PAPER, WITH THE OLD PROCEDURE DESCRIBED: **THIS DIFFERS FROM THE APPROACH ADOPTED IN 2015**, which used a Galactic dust template **WITH THE SAME SHAPE AT ALL FREQUENCIES**. The superseded choice is named, so the two releases' numbers can be read as answers to slightly different questions
span.quote: This differs from the approach adopted in 2015, which used a Galactic dust template with the same shape at all frequencies.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A COINED ACRONYM IS MINTED FOR OBJECTS THE ANALYSIS ITSELF PRODUCES, AND THE RULE THAT DECIDES HOW MANY OF THEM COUNT IS LEFT UNNAMED: the rotation diagonalizing the Fisher inverse **DEFINES** the eigenmodes; truncation of the hierarchy, to determine the number used for parameter estimation, is performed **ACCORDING TO SOME SUITABLY CHOSEN SELECTION CRITERION** - **AND WE REFER TO THESE MODES AS “EXEMS”**. One sentence defines the objects, the next leaves the rule for counting them to be chosen suitably, and the third gives them a name
span.quote: The rotation diagonalizing the Fisher inverse defines the xe eigenmodes. Truncation of the eigenmode hierarchy to determine the number of xe modes used for parameter estimation is performed according to some suitably chosen selection criterion. We refer to these modes as “eXeMs”

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A DISAGREEMENT IS LEFT OPEN WITH ITS THREE POSSIBLE MEANINGS ENUMERATED AND NONE CHOSEN: further work is needed to assess whether the discrepancy **IS A STATISTICAL FLUCTUATION, IS CAUSED BY SMALL SYSTEMATIC ERRORS, OR IS A SIGNATURE OF NEW PHYSICS**. Noise, error, and discovery are offered as the alternatives, in that order, and the paper declines to rank them
span.quote: Further work is needed to assess whether the discrepancy between Planck and the Ly α BAO results is a statistical fluctuation, is caused by small systematic errors, or is a signature of new physics.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN ASSUMPTION IS JUSTIFIED BY WHAT THE SIMPLEST MODELS PREDICT, WITH THE PRECISION CAVEAT IN A PARENTHESIS: the base model assumes that the spatial hypersurfaces are flat, **SUCH AS WOULD BE PREDICTED (TO WITHIN MEASURABLE PRECISION) BY THE SIMPLEST INFLATIONARY MODELS**. The warrant for the assumption is the simplicity of a theory, and the hedge is about what an instrument could see
span.quote: The base-ΛCDM model assumes that the spatial hypersurfaces are flat, such as would be predicted (to within measurable precision) by the simplest inflationary models.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A FEATURE THAT PULLS PARAMETERS AWAY FROM THE MODEL IS REPORTED **AND REBUTTED IN THE SAME SENTENCE**, BY NAMING THE PROBES THAT DO NOT SEE IT: a feature which pulls some parameters that affect the lensing amplitude away from the model; **HOWEVER, THIS IS NOT SUPPORTED BY THE LENSING RECONSTRUCTION OR** (in models that also change the background geometry) **BAO DATA**. The anomaly's own paper supplies the evidence against it
span.quote: which pulls some parameters that affect the lensing amplitude away from the ΛCDM model; however, this is not supported by the lensing reconstruction or (in models that also change the background geometry) BAO data.

span.label: a >2-sigma feature pulls some lensing-amplitude parameters away from the model, not supported by other probes
span.note: what this limits: the lensing-amplitude parameters specifically: a >2-sigma feature PULLS SOME PARAMETERS THAT AFFECT THE LENSING AMPLITUDE AWAY FROM THE [model], unsupported by other probes
span.quote: which pulls some parameters that affect the lensing amplitude away from the ΛCDM model;

span.label: Residual systematic errors in the polarization spectra are not folded into the quoted error bars, because the authors judge any such characterisation would be incomplete and could not be given a proper probabilistic form.
span.note: what this limits: every quoted uncertainty in the paper: WE THEREFORE DO NOT EXPLICITLY MODEL AN INCREASE IN ERROR BARS DUE TO THESE RESIDUAL SYSTEMATIC ERRORS - a known error source is excluded by decision
span.quote: In this paper we therefore do not explicitly model an increase in error bars due to these residual systematic errors – any such characterization would inevitably be incomplete, and it would also be impossible to give the necessary probabilistic characterization required for meaningful quantitative error bars.

span.label: Imperfect corrections for polarization efficiency and temperature-to-polarization leakage remain the dominant systematic error in the high-multipole polarization spectra.
span.note: what this limits: the polarization results in particular: INACCURACIES IN THE CORRECTIONS FOR EFFECTIVE POLARIZATION EFFICIENCIES AND TEMPERATURE-TO-POLARIZATION LEAKAGE ARE THE MAIN CONTRIBUTORS TO SYSTEMATIC ERRORS
span.quote: Inaccuracies in the corrections for effective polarization efficiencies and temperature-to-polarization leakage are the main contributors to systematic errors in the Planck polarization spectra at high multipoles.

span.label: The origin of the disagreement between Planck and the Lyman-alpha BAO measurements is left unresolved.
span.note: what this limits: the Planck-versus-Lyman-alpha comparison: FURTHER WORK IS NEEDED TO ASSESS WHETHER THE DISCREPANCY ... IS A STATISTICAL FLUCTUATION, IS CAUSED BY SMALL SYSTEMATIC ERRORS, OR IS A SIGNATURE OF new physics
span.quote: Further work is needed to assess whether the discrepancy between Planck and the Ly α BAO results is a statistical fluctuation, is caused by small systematic errors, or is a signature of new physics.

span.label: Residual modelling uncertainty in the small-scale polarization is estimated, not eliminated, and is stated to shift parameters at the half-sigma level.
span.note: what this limits: the small-scale polarization constraints: RESIDUAL MODELLING UNCERTAINTIES ESTIMATED TO AFFECT THEM ONLY AT THE 0.5 SIGMA L[evel] - estimated, not eliminated
span.quote: Improved modelling of the small-scale polarization leads to more robust constraints on many parameters, with residual modelling uncertainties estimated to affect them only at the 0.5σ level.

span.label: The choice of which external data to combine with is justified partly by a presentational aim, not only an evidential one.
span.note: what this limits: the external-data selection as a purely evidential choice: the paper gives as its second reason that its primary purpose is to present and emphasize the Planck results
span.quote: Secondly, the primary purpose of this paper is to present and emphasize the Planck results. We therefore make minimal use of external

span.label: The likelihood used for the 2018 analysis was built on a fiducial model taken from the previous data release.
span.note: what this limits: the 2018 parameter constraints as independent of the 2015 analysis: the likelihood was constructed using a fiducial model adopted from PCP15
span.quote: we need to adopt a fiducial model. For the 2018 analysis, we adopted the best-fit CamSpec base-ΛCDM model from PCP15 to construct a likelihood from the 2018 temperature maps.

span.label: Cluster counts are excluded from the main parameter grid because their mass calibrations are uncertain.
span.note: what this limits: these constraints as incorporating cluster counts: they are deliberately excluded from the main parameter grid
span.quote: Given the uncertainties in these calibrations, we do not use cluster counts in our main parameter grid.

span.label: The headline late-Universe parameters are marked model-dependent in a single parenthesis - 'the inferred (model-dependent) late-Universe parameters are: Hubble constant H0 = ...' - while the angular acoustic scale in the preceding sentence is described as only weakly model-dependent. Two classes of number sit in one abstract with very different warrants, separated by one bracketed word that does not survive being quoted.
span.quote: Assuming the base-ΛCDM cosmology, the inferred (model-dependent) late-Universe parameters are: Hubble constant H0 = (67.4 ± 0.5) km s−1 Mpc−1; matter density parameter Ωm = 0.315 ± 0.007; and matter fluctuation amplitude σ8 = 0.811 ± 0.006.

span.label: covariance matrices
span.quote: To construct covariance matrices, temperature-topolarization leakage corrections, and effective polarization efficiencies, we need to adopt a fiducial model. For the 2018 analysis, we adopted the best-fit CamSpec base-ΛCDM model from PCP15 to construct a likelihood from the 2018 temperature maps. We then ran a minimizer on the TT likelihood, imposing a prior of τ = 0.05 ± 0.02, and the best-fit base-ΛCDM cosmology was adopted as our fiducial model.

span.label: polarization efficiencies
span.quote: This is clearly a model-dependent procedure, but given that we fit over a restricted range of multipoles, where the T T spectra are measured to cosmic variance, the resulting polarization calibrations are insensitive to small changes in the underlying cosmological model.

span.label: Hubble constant
span.quote: Distance-ladder measurements of the Hubble constant, H0, are an exception, however. The latest measurement from Riess et al. (2019) is discrepant with the Planck base- ΛCDM value for H0 at about the 4.4σ level.

span.label: polarization angles → efficiencies
span.note: THE TWO CANNOT BE SEPARATED IN THIS STUDY - the DESIGN form of the negative relation (Q-286/Q-287). No edge type can express it: all eight assert that a relation HOLDS. Recorded here because a confounding statement BOUNDS WHAT THE PAPER'S OWN RESULTS CAN MEAN, and it lives in a methods paragraph where nothing downstream will find it. States the mechanism of the inseparability in one word - DEGENERATE - which is the physics term for exactly the relation we cannot express.
span.quote: The SRoll mapmaking algorithm assumes the ground-based measurements of polarization angles and efficiencies, which cannot be separated because they are degenerate with each other.

span.label: late-Universe parameter - a quantity the paper marks parenthetically as MODEL-DEPENDENT, inferred by assuming base-LambdaCDM rather than measured directly
span.quote: the inferred (model-dependent) late-Universe parameters are: Hubble constant H0 = (67.4 ± 0.5) km s−1 Mpc−1; matter density parameter Ωm = 0.315 ± 0.007; and matter fluctuation amplitude

span.quote: We find good consistency with the standard spatially-flat 6-parameter ΛCDM cosmology having a power-law spectrum of adiabatic scalar perturbations (denoted “base ΛCDM” in this paper), from polarization, temperature, and lensing, separately and in combination.

span.label: polarization efficiencies - AS CALIBRATED: by a procedure the paper itself calls model-dependent, and then BOUNDS rather than defends - the fit is restricted to multipoles where the TT spectra are cosmic-variance limited, which is the reason given for the calibration being insensitive to small changes in the cosmology
span.quote: This is clearly a model-dependent procedure, but given that we fit over a restricted range of multipoles, where the T T spectra are measured to cosmic variance, the resulting polarization calibrations are insensitive to small changes in the underlying cosmological model.

span.label: contradicts → Riess et al. (2019) distance-ladder measurement of the Hubble constant
span.quote: The latest measurement from Riess et al. (2019) is discrepant with the Planck base- ΛCDM value for H0 at about the 4.4σ level.

span.label: covariance matrices —operationalised-as→ fiducial model
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE LIKELIHOOD IS BUILT FROM THE MODEL IT IS LATER USED TO CONSTRAIN, IN TWO STEPS AND IN THE OPEN. 'To construct covariance matrices, temperature-topolarization leakage corrections, and effective polarization efficiencies, WE NEED TO ADOPT A FIDUCIAL MODEL. For the 2018 analysis, we adopted the best-fit CamSpec base-ΛCDM model FROM PCP15' - the PREVIOUS data release - 'to construct a likelihood from the 2018 temperature maps. We then ran a minimizer on the TT likelihood ... and the best-fit base-ΛCDM cosmology was adopted as our fiducial model.' So the 2018 fiducial descends from the 2015 fiducial by refitting. Nothing is concealed; the loop is simply not visible in any parameter value it produces.
span.quote: To construct covariance matrices, temperature-topolarization leakage corrections, and effective polarization efficiencies, we need to adopt a fiducial model. For the 2018 analysis, we adopted the best-fit CamSpec base-ΛCDM model from PCP15 to construct a likelihood from the 2018 temperature maps. We then ran a minimizer on the TT likelihood, imposing a prior of τ = 0.05 ± 0.02, and the best-fit base-ΛCDM cosmology was adopted as our fiducial model.

span.label: Hubble constant —operationalised-as→ base-ΛCDM
span.note: differs in: WHETHER H0 IS MEASURED OR INFERRED. One number comes from a distance ladder built out of local objects; the other is what base-ΛCDM requires given the CMB. 'The latest measurement from Riess et al. (2019) is discrepant with the PLANCK BASE-ΛCDM VALUE for H0 at about the 4.4σ level' - the paper's own wording keeps the model attached to its number, and the abstract marks the whole class parenthetically: 'the inferred (MODEL-DEPENDENT) late-Universe parameters' · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE MOST CITED DISAGREEMENT IN COSMOLOGY IS BETWEEN A MEASUREMENT AND A MODEL-CONDITIONAL INFERENCE, and the marker that says so is one parenthesis in an abstract. Strip the parenthesis and two numbers with error bars appear to contradict each other directly.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201833910.
